questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: What do headers do?

options.text: Protect the driver during a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver during a crash
questions.explanation: Headers protect the driver from cargo moving forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should make sure the ____ engage automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should engage automatically when air tank pressure falls between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and releasing air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve will pop out and spring brakes will engage.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, your main braking method should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking through downshifting.
questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Slow down and shift to a lower gear before you start going down the hill.

questions.question: You can tell a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) by looking for:

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate on the inside of the driver's side door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with ABS has a yellow ABS warning light on the instrument panel.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes.
questions.correctAnswerText: Modulating control valve
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver apply spring brakes slowly. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to maximize your time.
Is a distraction to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction to the driver.
questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention off the road and requires you to remove one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: ____ is required emergency equipment.
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: After changing a tire and driving a short distance, you should stop to:

options.text: Make sure the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is wearing evenly.
Make sure the tire air pressure is correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you drive a short distance with a new tire, stop and recheck that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: What is black ice?
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road shows through it and looks wet. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic light

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before each trip. If you have a trailer, make sure it is straight when you adjust your mirrors.

questions.question: Driving in very hot weather:

options.text: Requires you to remove oil from the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can increase tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Very hot weather causes air in your tires to expand. This increases tire pressure to dangerous levels. Keep enough oil and coolant in your engine to prevent overheating.

questions.question: Not draining the tanks in an air brake system can cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much fuel to be carried.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: You must drain the air storage tanks in an air brake system to remove water and oil buildup. If water stays in the system, it can freeze in cold weather and cause your brakes to fail.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Unless you are about to hit something, do not brake until your vehicle has slowed down enough.

questions.question: How much water on a road causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water instead. It does not take much water for this to happen.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should ensure all of the following, except:

options.text: The cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is balanced and properly secured. Keep weight as low as possible to prevent rollovers. Do not overload the truck.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks are hazardous because:

options.text: People rushing to exit may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People rushing to exit may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are risky because drivers may be in a hurry. They might pull into traffic without warning or step out without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: When using road speed to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Read your vehicle's manual to learn which speeds work for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up when you reach the top speed for your current gear.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during inspection?

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is still there.
The driver must reduce the weight of the load.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service. It cannot be driven until the spring is fixed.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which task will you NOT be required to do?

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: To pass the CDL inspection test, you must walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, what happens if one system loses pressure?

options.text: The other system will send air to help the low system.
The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
The low system will use a backup system to fill the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. You should stop your vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test, where should your vehicle end up?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete the exercise exactly as instructed, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: When using controlled braking in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes with about half of your normal force.
Apply the brakes so the wheels lock.
Apply the brakes with light pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep your steering wheel movements small when braking this way.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, what is the maximum air leakage rate during an applied leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 4 psi per minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure per minute during an applied leakage test. Know the safe leakage rate for your vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating located?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door.
On the side of each tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does it mean if other vehicles are not spraying water?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is stuck under the vehicles.
The tires have absorbed all the moisture.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles are not spraying water, ice has formed. Drive slowly and carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: During an inspection, how much can slack adjusters on S-cam brakes move?
questions.correctAnswerText: One inch.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check that it does not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, the brakes need adjustment.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It distracts your mind and your hands.
A message may upset the driver.
People become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts your mind and your hands.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it is both a mental and physical distraction. It takes your attention away from the road and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: How far ahead should you scan the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds ahead.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards and react before you reach them. Look for vehicles entering the highway or changing lanes.

questions.question: How do you remove water and compressor oil from the bottom of an air storage tank?

options.text: Siphon the water and oil out of the tank.
Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
The water and oil are removed automatically when the brakes are used.
Use a sponge to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
questions.explanation: Use a drain valve to remove water and oil from air storage tanks. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. You must drain manually operated tanks every day.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
Use any extinguisher on any type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
questions.explanation: Stay far from the fire and aim the extinguisher at the base of the fire, not the flames. Water may work on some fires. If you are not sure how to treat a fire, wait for trained firefighters.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both tanks. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: If you transport hazardous materials that require placards, you must:

options.text: Ask permission from local law enforcement.
Transport the materials only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials requiring placards, you need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: Too little weight on a steering axle can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Poor traction.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be balanced so it does not affect safe handling. If cargo is too far back, the front axle becomes too light. The front wheels will not have enough grip for safe steering.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Eight to nine hours
questions.explanation: Good rest is critical for safe vehicle operation. Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually notices hazards more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see road hazards more slowly than focused drivers, or they may not see them at all.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should weight be placed?
questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. If cargo is too high, the vehicle may tip over.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver can:

options.text: Use any cell phone while driving.
Use only a hands-free phone while driving.
Use a cell phone on rural roads only.
Use a cell phone at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only a hands-free phone while driving.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers cannot use hand-held phones while driving.

questions.question: Dual tires should touch each other.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put weight evenly balanced over the axles.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put weight evenly balanced over the axles.
questions.explanation: Load cargo must be balanced properly. Too much weight on an axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight on an axle reduces traction and makes handling difficult.

questions.question: When a construction worker is near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In work zones, drive at posted speed limits. Slow down even more when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: When speeding up on a slippery surface like a wet road, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Speed up very gradually when driving on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.question: If a truck has one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops a tractor-trailer from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: During an inspection, make sure your brake pads are:

options.text: Clean and free of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean and free of oil and grease.
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, check for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Does not change how you apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change how you apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) works with your braking system to prevent brake lock-up during hard braking. Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without it. ABS may not shorten your stopping distance.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Keep full air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
Must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
Do not need time to build air pressure before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection part of the skills test, you must:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show your knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection skills test, explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Your stopping distance is affected by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are driving. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Needed to carry both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed to carry both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to operate a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases.
